pack.title: Contractors quotes
pack.description: Check an additional cost before agreeing.

scenarios.setting: A contractor proposes an extra charge after starting the agreed job.
scenarios.jab: It's only another five hundred; we might as well do it now.
scenarios.goal: Check an additional cost before agreeing.

replies.line: Send the scope and price in writing before any additional work.
replies.why: It creates a clear approval step before the cost is incurred.
replies.delivery: Stress “before,” speak slowly, and keep the request focused on written scope.

replies.line: Written quote first. No extra work yet.
replies.why: It pauses the change until its terms are explicit.
replies.delivery: Say “Written quote first” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. And keep the request focused on written scope.

replies.line: Could you itemize the change so I can review it before we proceed?
replies.why: It asks for enough detail to make an informed decision.
replies.delivery: Stress “before,” speak slowly, and keep the request focused on written scope.

replies.line: My budget likes its surprises in birthday cards.
replies.why: Humor communicates the need for predictable costs without attacking the contractor.
replies.delivery: Keep “My budget likes its surprises in birthday cards” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. And keep the request focused on written scope.

followUp.line: Please explain the schedule impact in the written quote; I still need to approve it.
followUp.why: It considers the timing while keeping the approval boundary intact.
followUp.delivery: Pause before “Please explain the schedule impact in the written quote,” keep the volume even, then allow an answer without reopening your decision.
